name: Dual-layer opposite-rotation vector morph pad with filter-drive LFO
goal: Build a lush evolving pad from two vector (4-corner XY) oscillators: same four portable shapes on both layers, layer B pitched up (~+12–13 st / +24–25 st on some corners for air), XY indexes modulated by one slow synced LFO but with opposite rotation directions per layer, long pad amp attack/release, then a mild driven low-pass whose drive is breathed by a second slow LFO, plus light ensemble and master reverb.
prerequisites: Vector / 4-wave XY oscillator (or the vector-xy-four-oscillator-crossfade-blend skill)
Two layers or two vector osc slots with independent XY modulation polarity
Filter with drive; ensemble/chorus; reverb send

inputs.name: corner_set
inputs.description: Four original/free shapes (e.g. sine, stretched complex, drone-ish, soft vocal-ish WT) — do not use proprietary bank names

inputs.name: vector_lfo_rate
inputs.description: Synced slow rate (tutorial ~4 bars) for XY motion

outputs.name: monster_vector_pad
outputs.description: Dual-layer opposite-vector pad with slow filter-drive motion and space FX

constraints: Map any named factory/SFZ waveforms in the source video to original/free equivalents; do not redistribute proprietary packs.
Not affiliated with SynthMaster. Portable to Traveler/Polyrhythm-style dual osc + mod matrix + FX bus.
Watch master gain when adding filter drive/distortion — drive raises perceived level.

steps.action: Create vector oscillator A with four contrasting portable waves in the corners; set pitch display to semitones. Keep all four corners at the same base pitch for a coherent chord tone.
steps.expect: Four-corner vector voice at one pitch

steps.action: Park the XY near a musically useful corner (tutorial favored a top-side start). Assign one slow synced sine LFO (~4 bars) to both X and Y indexes with opposite polarities/amounts so the path orbits (left-right on one axis, up-down on the other) instead of only sliding on a diagonal.
steps.expect: Timbre slowly circles rather than teleporting between opposite corners

steps.action: Copy oscillator A settings to oscillator/layer B. Pitch two corners ~+13 st (octave-ish) and another ~+25 st (two octaves) for depth/air while leaving structural corners nearer the base if needed. Invert the XY modulation directions so B orbits the opposite way (clockwise vs anticlockwise) from the same LFO.
steps.expect: Two layers thicken; motion feels counter-rotating

steps.action: Shared pad amp envelope on both parts: long attack (pull attack curve back), decay ~9 o'clock, sustain as-is, release ~3 o'clock (release doubles as a soft tail). Lengthen attack further if the swell should feel glacial.
steps.expect: Notes fade in and wash out without a pluck

steps.action: One analog-style low-pass on the layer: moderate cutoff (~12–1 o'clock), no resonance, standard key track, tiny static drive. Modulate filter drive from a second synced LFO (triangle, different phase/rate than the vector LFO) with only a small positive depth so drive washes in gently.
steps.expect: Subtle grit breathes without constant distortion

steps.action: Optional: second envelope → cutoff with some decay and sustain at zero for a slow open that uses decay/release. Insert light ensemble on one FX slot; send master reverb (aftertouch→reverb amount is optional). Ride master volume down whenever drive/distortion is added.
steps.expect: Wide, evolving pad that stays mixable

verification: Solo A vs B: opposite XY orbit directions are audible as counter-motion.
Amp attack is clearly pad-like; release tails without a click.
Filter-drive LFO adds intermittent warmth, not constant fuzz; peak levels stay controlled.
